newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian president expected to name PM candidate.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian president expected to name PM candidate.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan started a third round of talks with parliamentary parties on Monday to decide on a prime minister for a new goverment following November's inconclusive general election.
The president's bureau said Kucan would make a statement afterwards.
"It is expected he will name a candidate then," Kucan's spokeswoman Spela Furlan told Reuters.

Kucan, who must name a candidate by January 3, has to decide between current Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats and head of the conservative People's Party Marjan Podobnik.

The Liberal Democrats are the strongest single party with 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats, while the People's Party is the largest of three rightist parties in a so-called "Spring" alliance. The group holds 45 seats, just one short of an absolute majority.
Once the president has named a candidate, parliament has to vote on the choice within seven days.
